title: Lightsheet Microscope Acquisition
author: Marda Jorgensen

One can use a refractometer to confirm the target refractive index (R.I.) of n = 1.45. Prepare a volume of solution at least 10 times that of the tissue being incubated. Prepare 63% TDE, a refractive index matching solutions (RIMS). Prepare a 63% 2,2'-thiodiethanol (TDE) solution, diluted with 1xPBS adjusted to pH 7.2. One can use a refractometer to confirm the target refractive index (R.I.) of n = 1.45. Prepare a volume of solution at least 10 times that of the tissue being incubated. Mix the solution gently to avoid creating bubbles.

steps.title: Incubate Tissue in TDE
steps.instruction: Incubate the cleared tissue sample in 63% TDE at room temperature with gentle agitation (rocking or rotating) for at least 1 hour or until the tissue sinks to the bottom of the tube.

substeps.instruction: Add a sufficient volume of 63% TDE to a clean tube.
Add the cleared tissue sample to the tube.
Avoid creating bubbles during this stage to ensure the sample sinks.

steps.title: Rinse Tissue
steps.instruction: Briefly rinse the tissue with 1x PBS to remove excess TDE.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the tissue to a clean surface.
Rinse briefly with 1x PBS.

steps.title: Prepare Glass Capillary
steps.instruction: Prepare the glass capillary for mounting by applying adhesive.

substeps.instruction: Set a glass capillary into the Sample Holder.
Dip the capillary into cyanoacrylate and set aside momentarily.

steps.title: Adhere Tissue to Capillary
steps.instruction: Mount the R.I. matched tissue to the prepared glass capillary.

substeps.instruction: Place the tissue on the rim of a weigh-boat.
Use forceps to stabilize the tissue and wick away excess liquid from the adhesion surface with a Kim Wipe.
Join the glued end of the glass capillary to the dried surface of the tissue.
Allow the glue to set before moving the sample.
Apply additional glue around the interface using another glass capillary if necessary.
Ensure the tissue hangs straight down from the capillary.

steps.title: Remove Microbubbles
steps.instruction: Remove microscopic bubbles to prevent shadow artifacts by dipping the sample briefly into 80% isopropanol/PBS.

substeps.instruction: Perform a 2-3 second dip.
Gently flick the sample holder during the dip.

steps.title: Mount Sample in Microscope
steps.instruction: Lower the mounted sample into the lightsheet microscope Sample Chamber, which must be pre-filled with 63% TDE.

steps.title: Align Tissue Angle
steps.instruction: Align the tissue to a 45-degree angle relative to the illumination/objective plane.

substeps.instruction: Zoom out fully to gauge tissue shape and alignment.

steps.title: Set Z-Stack Slices
steps.instruction: Define the first and last planes of the z-stack.

substeps.instruction: Progress the tissue to locate the furthest edge in focus along the z-axis and select it as the first plane.
Repeat the process for the opposite side of the tissue to set the last plane.

steps.title: Determine X and Y Bounds
steps.instruction: Designate the bounding region for sequential z-stack acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Record the upper and lower Y-axis values from the specimen navigator panel.
Repeat the process for each X-axis value.

steps.title: Assign Multiview Bounds
steps.instruction: Set the top-left and bottom-right bounds in the multiview panel using the specimen navigator.

substeps.instruction: Move sample to the top-left most region (upper y-axis and lower x-axis values) and add to the multiview panel.
Repeat for the lower-right most region.
Ensure regions account for the entire z-stack scanning range of tissues at various angles.

steps.title: Generate Multiview Z-Stacks
steps.instruction: Use Zeiss TileStitcher to populate Multiview positions for the entire tissue volume.

substeps.instruction: Save Multiview positions and load them into Zeiss TileStitcher.
Select the bounding box feature and set the scan to meander mode.
Enter imaging size parameters: Image Size, number of Slices, and % overlap.
Save and load the autopopulated z-stack Multiview coordinates into the acquisition software's Multiview panel.
Record the count of z-stacks along the x and y axes.

steps.title: Adjust Laser Sheet Angles
steps.instruction: Tune the laser objective angles to account for R.I. mismatch and ensure the clearest live image.

substeps.instruction: Select either the left or right side laser and adjust the angle in the Illumination Parameters panels.
Visually inspect the live feed and adjust until the image is clearest.
Note the alignment angle and test multiple points in the z-stack range to confirm the adjustment is appropriate for the bulk of the tissue.
Repeat the process for the opposing laser sheet.

steps.title: Reconcile Dual-Sided Illumination
steps.instruction: Fine-tune the left and right laser alignment so that both have the same focal plane and features appear in the same location.

substeps.instruction: Check alignment across various regions of the tissue volume.

steps.title: Configure Acquisition Settings
steps.instruction: Set the laser and acquisition parameters for imaging.

substeps.instruction: For autofluorescence imaging: use a 488 excitation laser at 90% power with 30ms exposure times.
Enable dual-sided acquisition and online dual-sided fusion.
Enable pivot scan.
Click 'Start Experiment'.
Designate a file name and directory location, then click 'Save'.
